issue_context.title: Some setting values without limit could cause crash
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.2.beta5.official [4c96e9676]

### System information

Godot v4.2.beta5 - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated Radeon RX 5500 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.14057.5006) - AMD FX(tm)-6300 Six-Core Processor (6 Threads)

### Issue description

There's a number of project settings, that has no limit for possible values range. In some cases, setting invalid value (mostly zero or negative) could cause editor crash on project open or game crash on start.
I suppose such limitation should be added (also it was in 3.x at least for some of them).

I created a commit that fixes this issue by adding PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE to forbid negative or zero values. But using PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE also has highest value limit, which is unknown to me without knowledge of engine internals. Because of that, I created this issue report instead of PR, to discuss values correctness. Please take a look:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...gshadows:godot:fix_options_range

Example of possible values is on image below. I found this bug when actually set some of such options to -1 accidentally.
![Example of invalid values](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/18046412/662e3113-29e0-4985-af7b-4ce2cec28636)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create empty project or open existing (assuming you have backup).
2. Open project settings and enable Advanced Settings (not all affected settings are advanced, this is just a good example).
3. Select "Reflections" and set any values as on image above, for example roughness layers = -1.
4. After project save and attempt to re-open, editor will crash.
5. The only way to recover is manual edit of project.godot (or restore from backup/vcs).

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
The values in the commit look good to me. I'd remove `or_greater` from all the reflection settings though, as huge values outside the specified range are unsupported by GPUs or are extremely slow. Same for the global shader variables buffer size.

On the other hand, the 2D/3D navigation cell size properties may actually warrant having `or_greater` for large-scale games (such as planetary simulations).
Thank you for review! I've updated code according recommendations and created PR.

review_comments: Unsure if this should be `or_greater`, for performance considerations

I'm not experienced in engine internals. That's why I was unsure about what exact values should be an upper limits. Initially I added `or_greater` almost everywhere because assumed it safer then creating limit and then find that someone actually used larger value.
If you know exact upper limit values or could confirm here 2048 is good top value I will remove `or_greater`. Thanks!

I have no clue, was just pointing out since it seems like a pretty performance critical thing given occlusion and threads 

CC @clayjohn any idea?

This value gets clamped internally between `viewport_size.x * viewport_size.y / (32 * 32)` and `viewport_size.x * viewport_size.y / (2 * 2)` after being multiplied by the number of threads. For a 1080x1920 screen with a CPU that supports 8 threads, the theoretical min is 254 and the theoretical max is 64,800.

For a 32 thread machine, it becomes 64 and 16,200. 

With a 4K monitor, the theoretical limits are much higher (with 8 threads, min is 1013, max is 259,200)

Accordingly, it makes sense to use `or_greater`
